content.comment_body: Hello, could someone assist? I'm unable to transfer a program that includes message texts from my PC to [product_name]. The download fails and details are shown in a window.
The information provided is quite limited. Is there an error message? If so, what does it say? Have you finished configuring all blocks in your program?

I responded too quickly earlier since your post changed. When transferring a program to [product_name], if an error occurs, an icon appears at the bottom right. Click the icon to open an information window where you'll find an explanation for the error.
[user_name], thanks for the details. Your explanation helped me. I was able to attach a text message in the program, then transfer it from PC to [product_name].

Good day, sorry for bringing up an old thread, but I don't fully understand the solution. I have the same error and can't download to my [product_name]. The info window indicates my text messages aren't connected to outputs, but I can't connect them to anything, as I just want them to appear on the [product_name] operator device. Any help would be appreciated. Thank you in advance.

Hello [user_name], if you see an error about message texts not being linked to an output, you need to connect them with outputs. This works similar to using open connectors. Could you upload your program to the forum (zipped) for review?
Thank you, I've uploaded the program. Is there any literature available that explains this issue in detail?
You need to finalize each text message by adding an open connector, for example. The video attached demonstrates this process using an example.

OFF-TOPIC: I'm impressed with the compact file size of that video! ON-TOPIC: [user_name], it's good to see documentation in your program; many neglect this. The issue arises when using the ladder diagram instead of FBD. If you convert your ladder program to FBD, the problem becomes clear. In FBD, you can see the message block actually has an output that needs connection. The solution is shown in the video (please give a good rating to [user_name]). The 'X1' acts as a terminator, serving only to terminate the block's output. You can also use a flag or output if preferred. For best practice, connect all message outputs in parallel to one terminator (open connector). To review message instructions, run the simulator and check each message using the footprint icon. Has your issue been resolved?

Thank you very much for the support. Manuals and help files can only help so much; real experience is far more useful. This solved my issue. If anyone has further recommendations on improving my program, please feel free to send a private message. Yes, [user_name] = [user_name].
Thanks for your help. I had the same issue, and using the ladder diagram now makes it clear what needs to be done.

This is really frustrating—the problem isn't using ladder, but a bug in the ladder compiler with no output terminal on the ladder message block. It's unreasonable to have to convert to FBD, add the output connection, then switch back to ladder, which ruins the logical flow of code. Although this is an older thread, the current [product_name] software still has the same issue even after three years. Very disappointing [company_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users had trouble transferring programs with message texts between PC and [product_name] due to message text blocks not being connected to outputs. The error is flagged in the software, and connecting unused outputs to open connectors or terminators is necessary to resolve the issue. Documentation was found lacking compared to practical advice from other users, and the issue was ultimately fixed by following peer guidance on proper workflow.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] software and hardware to support program transfer even when message text blocks are only for display and not linked to logical outputs. They also wish for clearer documentation on necessary connections and error management.
